Getting Started > Adopting Verse for Games and Hosting It in Plugins
Status: positioning record (2026-10-29, decided by the user). This page registers the upgraded positioning of the Verse feature set, upgraded because the premise "it will serve games in the future" changed, and its plugin hosting form; the implementation schedule follows the ordering chain fixed in section nine of document 13, and the Verse research facts are in section two of document 16.

1. The Premise Change: From "Observe Only" to Full Adoption in the Long Term

Decided by the user (2026-10-29): this ecosystem's SA / SLA may in the future have to serve games. In document 16, Jev's ruling on "online prediction / parallel STM" was observe only (0.86), but that ruling was built on an explicit premise — our deliverables do no online prediction. That premise has now changed, and the ruling's foundation fails with it: the Verse feature set's positioning is upgraded from "observe only" to a long-term full adoption target.

The adoption horizon is circled in full by the research facts in section two of document 16, regardless of shipped or unshipped: the shipped local failure-rollback transactions and function-signature effect annotations; the unreleased parallel STM (speculative execution + conflict retry) and <predicts> client prediction (client-side predictive running, server-authoritative correction). The latter does not yet exist as a formed mechanism on Epic's side; what is adopted is its design goals and semantic form, to be redesigned at landing time under our own runtime conditions — not a port of Epic's implementation.

2. Hosting Form: Hosted in Plugins, Split into Three Layers

The main session's proposal, approved by the user: the Verse set does not enter the SLA core; it is split by nature into three layers, each placed where it belongs.

  • The language semantics layer → a language plugin / dialect frontend. Failure-rollback semantics (writes inside a failure context are tentative and are revoked wholesale on failure) and decides / transacts-style circumscription of rollback-capable code are compiler semantics and cannot enter a runtime plugin. But the plugin system has long had a kind=language category: SLA and slars both hang on the host as language frontends, dispatched by the host by file extension. So the form = a Verse-oriented language plugin / dialect profile, under slars's hard conditions — do not move SLA; open a separate frontend; the lowering and codegen share the same code as SLA, landing likewise on SA; the SLA core is not polluted by game semantics.
  • The runtime engine layer → a domain plugin. The transaction speculation engine (write log / rollback) and the netcode skeleton for prediction and rollback (snapshot rings, input delay, rollback replay) are domain capabilities, not basic cores of the HTTP / TCP kind, so the "basic cores go into sa_std" placement does not apply. A ready precedent exists: the db plugin is exactly the form "domain engine + host registration". The existing game-oriented seed, sla_ecs, belongs under this line as the engine layer's existing starting point.
  • The general parts → the SLA core. Effect annotations hold for non-game scenarios too; they have already been adopted, per document 16's ruling (0.66), into the SLA goroutine syntax batch, following the core route and not going with the game profile — whether or not the game profile ever starts, this part lands as usual.

3. Boundaries

What is adopted is Verse's mechanisms (transaction speculation, prediction rollback, effect circumscription), not turning SLA into Verse: the syntax surface, checker discipline, and ownership model remain this ecosystem's own. The game profile is an optional mount — the code paths of the three servers (slanginx / slaredis / db) are never forced to carry the cost of speculative execution; if you do not use the game profile you pay not a single character for it. The SA specification remains frozen as usual: all three layers land in the upper layers and plugin surfaces outside sa_std, and do not conflict with the base decision.

4. Schedule

The whole program's master ordering (decided by the user on 2026-10-29): first complete the Erlang + goroutine complex (runtime phase one → the SLA syntax batch; ordering per documents 13 / 15 / 16), then complete the concurrency performance improvements of the three machines (slanginx / slaredis / db), and only after both are complete consider adding Verse and Haskell (STM etc.) features. So this line's starting gate is "the complex + the three-machine improvements both complete", not "start as soon as the complex is done". It is a long-term line. At present only the registered positioning changes; no construction surface is touched — the runtime phase one under construction, the already-scheduled syntax batch, and the three-machine rework are all unaffected by this page. The starting point and phasing (the order of the language profile and the engine layer, the circling of the first-phase semantic subset) are to be ruled on when the time comes.

Related discussions: Erlang Concurrency Candidates and a Verse Transaction Survey, The goroutine Runtime: Design Discussion on Bringing It into sa_std.
